title: On imperial legacies in knowledge building in China: a gweilo’s view
text_snippet: On imperial legacies in knowledge building in China: a gweilo’s view Abstract Asia as method: toward deimperialization argues for learning within and across Asia. As he argues, understanding the role of the west has led to an inapt and unhelpful, obsessive regard for the west, while regional Asian comparisons can be valuable to more understand the role of various forces across diverse historical and cultural locations. This paper responds in part to Chen’s by comparing how knowledge production is understood in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland. By comparing sites, this paper sheds light on the cultural nature of knowledge building. Furthermore, this paper takes on what the author calls a gweilo's view, engaging in self-reflection and self-criticism as advised by Chen in relation to one's own positionality as an insider/outsider in comparative scholarly work. The paper examines the nature of a gweilo perspective, before comparatively examining knowledge building norms and their historical roots in Hong Kong and the Chinese Mainland. It concludes with reflections and implications for ethical scholarly engagement in an intersectional, interconnected world.

title: ESD in higher education in the Philippines: policies shaped through international discourse and national realities
text_snippet: ESD in higher education in the Philippines: policies shaped through international discourse and national realities Abstract This study explores the narrative evolution of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) higher education policy in the Philippines up to its present conceptions. This is done through qualitative methods, namely a policy analysis through the Multiple Streams Framework (MSF), and semi-structured interviews with participants from the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), the Philippine National Commission for UNESCO (PH NATCOM), and a higher education institution (HEI). While the MSF is commonly used to explain policy change through moments of convergence, this study looks at non-convergence and the absence of a policy window in mainstreaming ESD in Philippine higher education governance. The policy analysis maps the problem, policy, and politics streams across time, grouping them into three distinct time periods: early (1977–1996), recent (2001–2010), and present (2011–2022). This study identifies a structural limitation of the MSF in executive-centred governance contexts, where political authority shapes both agenda-setting and institutional capacity that is required for coupling. title: Understanding professional vulnerability in the context of quality-oriented education system: experiences of homeroom teachers in mainland China
text_snippet: Understanding professional vulnerability in the context of quality-oriented education system: experiences of homeroom teachers in mainland China Abstract While teachers’ professional vulnerability has been increasingly investigated in various school settings across the globe, scant attention has been paid to homeroom teachers’ professional vulnerability in Chinese secondary education. Adopting a case study design and drawing upon a rich dataset comprising interviews, observations, and documents, the present study explored how three homeroom teachers from a junior middle school in mainland China perceived and coped with their professional vulnerability within the milieu of the quality-oriented education system. The findings unraveled the complexities of homeroom teachers’ professional vulnerability and revealed how sociocultural, institutional, and personal factors have affected their practical engagements, interpersonal relations, and emotional responses. The findings also showcased how homeroom teachers manage their vulnerability through coping strategies such as strategic reorientation, capacity-building, and self-protection. The study offers valuable insights for homeroom teachers and policymakers in China and other contexts.

title: Subverting educational hegemony through translation: the role of translated texts in fostering counter-hegemonic pedagogy in authoritarian academic contexts
text_snippet: Subverting educational hegemony through translation: the role of translated texts in fostering counter-hegemonic pedagogy in authoritarian academic contexts Abstract This study investigates the transformative potential of translated texts as tools for intellectual resistance and pedagogical innovation within authoritarian academic systems, focusing on Iran’s political science departments. Employing a qualitative, interpretative approach grounded in a synthetic theoretical framework, the research draws on semi-structured interviews with professors and lecturers from leading Iranian universities. The analysis identifies “hidden cultural codes” embedded in translated English texts that educators strategically utilize to repoliticize depoliticized curricula, foster critical inquiry, and nurture democratic values. Findings reveal that these texts serve as valuable educational resources that promote analytical engagement while also acting as vehicles of intellectual resistance that challenge state-imposed ideological constraints. By embedding alternative narratives of political agency and civic participation, translated works transform classrooms into spaces of quiet subversion, enabling students to critically interrogate power structures. title: Do it yourself tutoring in Cambodia: new directions in shadow education research
text_snippet: Do it yourself tutoring in Cambodia: new directions in shadow education research Abstract Covid-19 turbocharged the adoption of digital technologies in mainstream schools, which necessarily changed the shape of private supplementary tutoring as well. This article traces these dynamics in Cambodia, outlining the concept of Do It Yourself (DIY) Tutoring. DIY Tutoring is curriculum-linked learning outside of the classroom that a student engages with autonomously through digital platforms. The digital nature of DIY Tutoring allows for a level of flexibility and personalization uncommon in other forms of self-guided tutoring. Most importantly, DIY Tutoring alters the traditional understanding of the cost of tutoring from direct user-fees to also include indirect fees common in platform capitalism. The article reports on empirical evidence in Cambodia to articulate a framework of DIY Tutoring. Although this study focuses on Cambodia, adding to the literature on shadow education in the country, the concept of DIY Tutoring can be applied more widely, opening new directions in shadow education research.

title: Teaching security beyond borders: the DMZ as an educational landscape
text_snippet: Teaching security beyond borders: the DMZ as an educational landscape Abstract In civic education, the sense of security brought into discussions informs how students engage with public issues and make decisions. This study foregrounds interpreted security as a critical force in shaping civic responsibility and collective identity. To explore how security is narrated and curated through educational practice, the research turns to the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) as a site where competing meanings of security intersect. Adopting environmental security as a connecting thread, this study examines how national, environmental, and human security are interwoven in the educational framing of the DMZ within its unique geopolitical and ecological context. By engaging with the DMZ in curriculum, this research discusses how security might be addressed beyond the boundaries of limited in-group interests to confront the shared insecurities of diverse lives and communities.

title: Profiles of gifted science high school students and their academic self-concept and college major pursuits
text_snippet: Profiles of gifted science high school students and their academic self-concept and college major pursuits Abstract This study explored how gifted high school students perceived their academic self-concept and future college major intentions in schools where homogeneous grouping was implemented full-time throughout the academic year. Using survey responses from 389 gifted high school students, major findings included that mostly, the gifted students maintained favorable perceptions about their scholastic ability and considerations of college majors in STEM. Their academic self-concept significantly differed across the four latent profiles, whereas intentions to change college majors did not show statistically significant differences. The highest academic self-concept was found for the group with high levels of the need for cognition, mastery goal orientation, and resilience. In contrast, the lowest group was characterized by low need for cognition, low performance but high mastery goal orientations, and a minimal social comparison tendency. title: An invitation to theorise East Asian pedagogy: bodymind, dark consciousness, kata, and self-cultivation
text_snippet: An invitation to theorise East Asian pedagogy: bodymind, dark consciousness, kata, and self-cultivation Abstract Building on the theoretical work initiated by Komatsu and Rappleye (Comparative Education Review 61:269–297, 2017), this paper turns to the East Asian and Japanese theories of bodymind (body-mind unity) and learning as a possible theoretical resource for a new appraisal of East Asian pedagogy. To this end, the paper will first delve into the East Asian and Japanese theories of bodymind and learning, drawing on scholarship of comparative philosophers Thomas Kasulis and Robert Carter, Japanese philosopher Yasuo Yuasa, and educational philosopher Tadashi Nishihira. The theoretical account, assembled from these scholarly works, is then deployed in rereading three recent studies on Confucian pedagogical thoughts and practices, based in Edo-Japan, Taiwan and China, that cut across time and space in East Asia. Aligned with Chen’s (Asia as method, Duke University Press, 2010) call for ‘Asia as method,’ this cross-temporal and -regional inquiry is intended not only to solidify the theoretical account of East Asian bodymind and pedagogy but also to suggest a comparative methodology that foregrounds reginal inter-referencing as a mode of theorisation.

title: The competence-based approach as the international norm in higher education: the Tuning initiative in Central Asia
text_snippet: The competence-based approach as the international norm in higher education: the Tuning initiative in Central Asia Abstract The present article shows how the flagship EU-funded project acted as a transnational epistemic community in higher education. Based on the case study of the TuCAHEA consortium (2012–2015), the article reveals how the development of international norms is driven by the opinion of academic experts, based on their principled and causal beliefs. The qualitative content analysis of scholarly publications by the members of the TuCAHEA project reveals that European experts showed a more balanced view on the competence-based approach, while the Central Asian members of the project expressed less critical thinking about it. Furthermore, while the European experts focused on the societal needs, the Central Asian authors connected the competence-based approach with the education reform process in their countries. The findings reveal that the Tuning initiative is an epistemic community that supports the diffusion and acceptance of the competence-based approach as an international norm in higher education.

title: Educational design research as a form of teacher professional learning: a systematic review
text_snippet: Educational design research as a form of teacher professional learning: a systematic review Abstract This study examines teacher professional learning (PL) in Educational Design Research (EDR) through a systematic review, integrating bibliometric and thematic analysis of 168 peer-reviewed articles published between 2006 and 2024. The findings reveal a steady increase in research on teacher PL in EDR, with global contributions highlighting the field’s growing relevance and evolving methodologies. The study proposes a preliminary role–change model that theorises how EDR shapes teacher learning by tracing the roles teachers occupy, the practices through which they participate, and the changes that unfold. The review also identifies four co-existing layers of influence - personal, community, school, and external contextual factors - that simultaneously enable or constrain teacher learning. While offering valuable insights into key trends and themes, the study acknowledges the need for further empirical validation of the preliminary role-change model, particularly concerning the practitioner-researcher role.

title: #YouAreWelcomeHere? The two faces of American higher education toward Chinese international students
text_snippet: #YouAreWelcomeHere? The two faces of American higher education toward Chinese international students Abstract Driven by neoliberal ideology and the enduring social imaginary of the West, international education and degrees from Western universities are often perceived by students and their families as ideal pathways to global citizenship, language acquisition, and enhanced employability. However, despite these presumed benefits, U.S. universities frequently implement homogenizing institutional practices that marginalize Chinese students within the very spaces that claim to empower them. The study adopts Derrida’s hos(ti)pitality (a blend of hospitality and hostility) to expose how U.S. institutions simultaneously welcome and exclude Chinese students. It identifies three dominant institutional orientations: one-way cultural socialization that privileges White, middle-class norms; deficit and culturalist ideologies that pathologize Chinese students, and institutional indifference towards their safety and psychological well-being. Grounded in a critical, equity-oriented perspective, this study employs interactional ethnography to examine how institutional structures and discourses influence the experiences of Chinese students in U.S. universities. title: The impact of one-to-one technology for improving digital literacy at middle schools in South Korea
text_snippet: The impact of one-to-one technology for improving digital literacy at middle schools in South Korea Abstract The rapid digital transformation in education has necessitated an evaluation of the impact of technology-enhanced learning environments. This study examines the effects of one-to-one technology implementation on the digital literacy of middle school students in South Korea, focusing on the 2022 curriculum revision. The research employs a case study approach, analyzing data collected from two schools with varying levels of technological integration. Using pre- and post-surveys, interviews, and classroom observations, the study assesses changes in students’ digital literacy, including understanding and application of digital technology, digital mindset, digital thinking ability, and digital literacy practice. The findings indicate statistically significant improvements in digital thinking ability, particularly among students with higher academic achievement levels. However, disparities in teacher engagement and school infrastructure influenced the effectiveness of the one-to-one technology implementation. The study highlights the need for structured pedagogical strategies, teacher training, and curriculum integration to optimize the benefits of technology-enhanced education.

title: The important role of higher art education in promoting the sustainable development of aesthetic education in Chinese universities
text_snippet: The important role of higher art education in promoting the sustainable development of aesthetic education in Chinese universities Abstract In the global context of integrating sustainable development into education, aesthetic education in higher education institutions cultivates students’ aesthetic literacy and creative capabilities. Higher art education, as a core component, plays an irreplaceable role in promoting sustainability in this field, though its contributions remain insufficiently explored.1 This study investigates higher art education as a key driver of sustainable aesthetic education in universities through text mining and social network analysis of 2081 CNKI publications (1980–2024). Findings reveal thematic shifts, developmental trends, and multidimensional knowledge systems that provide theoretical foundations and practical pathways for sustainable aesthetic education.

title: Bullying victimization and school engagement: the role of subjective well-being
text_snippet: Bullying victimization and school engagement: the role of subjective well-being Abstract Efforts have been made to understand the underlying mechanism between bullying victimization and school engagement but primarily focused on the mediating effects of depression and anxiety, despite that low subjective well-being (SWB) is more commonly experienced among victims of school bullying. This study compared the mediating effects of SWB, depression, and anxiety in the association between bullying victimization and overall school engagement and examined how SWB was related to each dimension of school engagement with a sample of 232 Chinese adolescents (44.4% boys, age M = 14.4, SD = 1.1). The results showed that SWB was a stronger mediator than depression and anxiety in the association between bullying victimization and overall school engagement. Furthermore, SWB fully mediated the associations between bullying victimization and each of the five dimensions of school engagement. These findings suggest that being bullied may not directly lower one’s school engagement, but it significantly compromises one’s SWB, which then predicts decreases in school engagement across various dimensions.

title: AI chatbot design principles to enhance the collective efficacy in collaborative learning
text_snippet: AI chatbot design principles to enhance the collective efficacy in collaborative learning Abstract To support effective collaborative learning, it is essential to enhance collective efficacy and provide timely, tailored feedback throughout the learning process. However, it is often difficult for a single instructor to monitor multiple groups and deliver feedback that meets the specific needs of each team in real time. This study aims to develop and validate a systematic design for an AI chatbot that enhances collective efficacy in collaborative learning environments. The design will be devised by developing and validating design principles. The design-based research methodology was conducted to develop the design principles, which were then validated by experts and evaluated for usability. This process involved a review of relevant literature and case analysis, followed by expert validation and usability test to confirm the design principles’ validity. The final design principles are composed of four design elements— (1) support for group cohesion, (2) support for affective cohesion, (3) support for collaborative learning activities, and (4) facilitation of dialogue—and ten design principles. title: Profile analysis of students with reading comprehension difficulties
text_snippet: Profile analysis of students with reading comprehension difficulties Abstract The ultimate goal of reading is ‘comprehension,’ and students with reading comprehension difficulties exhibit an inappropriate level of comprehension ability considering their age. From this perspective, this study analyzed the cognitive profiles of sixth-grade students by using the fusion model of cognitive diagnostic model and examined different levels of students (good, average, struggling). In order to conduct this study, a reading comprehension test was conducted for 1000 sixth-grade students in 28 elementary schools in Seoul, Gyeonggi-do, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Gyeongsangnam-do, Busan, Gwangju and Jeju-do. As a result, good, average and struggling students in reading comprehension showed differences in the ability to master cognitive attributes. Especially, struggling readers were classified into five types according to three levels of comprehension, namely literal, inferential and evaluative comprehension. The cognitive diagnosis of these types serves as an important source of information for identifying students’ strengths and weaknesses, and it is significant in that it is a statistical analysis of the complicated process of reading comprehension.

title: Differentiated instruction: an investigation into the effect of class compositional factors on teaching processes
text_snippet: Differentiated instruction: an investigation into the effect of class compositional factors on teaching processes Abstract Class composition factors including class size and the grade or other level of students are often studied for their impact on factors such as academic outcomes and student achievement, but less often address the impacts on teachers’ instructional strategies. This paper reports on an analysis of the relationship between class compositional factors, including class size and level of study, on differentiated instruction (DI) in the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP). In the IBDP, students take subjects at Standard Level (SL) or Higher Level (HL), and it is a common practice to combine classes of SL and HL students within each subject, often because enrolment numbers are too small to make streamed classes viable. Examining the practices of teachers in IBDP schools in Hong Kong, this paper outlines a typology of teachers’ approaches to DI, highlighting the ways compositional factors impact upon teaching and learning and reflecting on the relationship between teacher beliefs and actions in DI in their senior secondary classrooms.

title: Exploring the relationship between sustainability and human rights: ecological transition education and its relevance to students’ human rights in South Korean education
text_snippet: Exploring the relationship between sustainability and human rights: ecological transition education and its relevance to students’ human rights in South Korean education Abstract This research explores the integrated dialectic between human rights education and education for sustainability in the context of global crises, including climate change and unexpected pandemics. The authors examine disparities between students’ rights and citizenship education in South Korean educational policies, questioning their lack of alignment concerning sustainability. To address this issue, we adopted a document analysis of two key educational policies introduced by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education (SMOE), South Korea: the Development Plan for Ecological Transition Education (implemented since 2020) and the Master Plan for Students’ Human Rights (implemented since 2018). These documents were analyzed through the lens of transformative education, specifically drawing on the Freirean ecopedagogy approach. Our analysis of the transformative educational dimensions embedded in these policies reveals a tendency to emphasize one aspect of citizenship for sustainability—either rights or responsibilities—rather than integrating both.
